title: Explainable artificial intelligence in clinical decision support systems: a systematic review of techniques, clinical applications, evaluation, and future directions.
authors: Zandkarimi E, Ghorbanzadeh K
abstract: BACKGROUND: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as an important approach for improving the transparency and interpretability of artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support systems (CDSSs). However, evidence regarding the models and explainability techniques used in healthcare, their clinical evaluation, methodological quality, and progression toward real-world implementation remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the current evidence on XAI-enabled CDSSs, with particular emphasis on AI and XAI methods, clinical applications, validation, explainability evaluation, implementation, and methodological limitations. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261449460). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from database inception through 30 June 2026 (searches run on 15 July 2026). Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles that applied artificial intelligence within healthcare clinical decision support systems, incorporated at least one explainability or interpretability technique, and demonstrated a direct role in clinical decision-making or decision support. Studies limited to prediction, classification, diagnosis, or prognostic modeling without a decision-support component were excluded. Two reviewers jointly screened titles and abstracts, independently assessed full texts, and independently extracted data using a standardized form informed by the CHARMS checklist. Risk of bias and applicability of prediction model studies were assessed using PROBAST, and reporting completeness was evaluated against relevant TRIPOD + AI recommendations where applicable. Due to substantial clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with SWiM guidance. RESULTS: Of 2008 identified records, 68 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Publications increased substantially in 2025-2026, accounting for 47 of the 68 included studies. China and India contributed the largest number of studies (11 each), followed by the United States (10). Critical care/intensive care medicine and cardiology were the most frequently represented clinical specialties (13 studies each). Numeric patient-level sample size was reported in 35 studies. Among these, the median sample size was 973 (IQR 303-10,015; range 57-106,449), while the mean was 11,944, indicating a markedly right-skewed distribution. Internal validation was reported in 51 studies (75.0 %), whereas external validation was reported in 17 studies (25.0 %). Most systems remained at the research-prototype stage (n = 63, 92.6 %). One study (1.5 %) reported pilot testing in a clinical workflow, while only two studies (2.9 %) reported real-world or routine clinical deployment. Implementation status was unclear or not reported in two studies (2.9 %). Of the 63 studies for which PROBAST was applicable, 3 (4.8 %) were judged at low overall risk of bias and 3 (4.8 %) at high risk; the remainder were rated Unclear mainly because of incomplete reporting. Five studies describing non-prediction CDSS designs were classified as PROBAST not applicable. Clinician involvement was reported in 53 studies. Formal user studies with structured evaluation protocols were reported in 39 studies (57.4 %), but rigorous assessment of effects on decision quality or patient outcomes remained rare. CONCLUSIONS: XAI-enabled CDSS research has expanded rapidly, yet remains largely confined to model development and technical explainability rather than rigorous clinical translation. Although SHAP and gradient-boosting methods currently predominate, external validation, real-world deployment, standardized evaluation of explanation quality, and meaningful human-centered assessment are still limited. Future work must prioritize multicenter external validation, transparent reporting, rigorous assessment of explanation fidelity and stability, active clinician and patient involvement, and prospective evaluation of effects on decision-making and patient outcomes. Closing the gap between algorithmic performance and clinically meaningful utility is essential for the safe, trustworthy, and responsible adoption of these systems.

title: Sex-dependent habenular dysregulation across the continuum of stress exposure and depression severity: A systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence.
authors: Ferreira-Vorkapic C, Coelho RR, Wiech M, Tocco F, Todde F
abstract: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is diagnosed at roughly twice the rate in women as in men, yet sex is still routinely treated as a covariate rather than a biological variable of primary interest in depression research. The habenula (Hb), particularly the lateral habenula (LHb), is an increasingly implicated substrate of depression, but two recent systematic reviews found sex-stratified habenula data sparse and reported sex effects inconsistent in direction. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether sex-related effects on habenula structure and function are patterned by stress intensity or chronicity in preclinical models, and by depression severity or chronicity in clinical populations, rather than arbitrary. METHODS: This review builds on two parent systematic reviews (Cameron, Weston-Green and Newell, 2024; Fortin et al., 2025), extracting eligible sex-stratified studies and supplementing them with an independent, two-phase search (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) for comprehensive coverage of sex- and stress-related terms. Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by stressor chronicity (preclinical) and illness chronicity or severity (clinical), without meta-analysis. RESULTS: Seventeen studies met eligibility criteria (10 preclinical, 7 clinical). In preclinical models, acute stressors produced modality-dependent, sometimes opposite-direction sex effects, while chronic stressors more consistently interacted with, and sometimes abolished, pre-existing baseline sex differences. In clinical populations, sex-dependent habenula abnormalities were largely absent in first-episode presentations and became more pronounced, often specifically in women, with greater illness chronicity, treatment resistance, or symptom severity. CONCLUSIONS: Sex-dependent habenula dysfunction in depression shows a patterned, chronicity-linked structure in both literatures, though the evidence base remains small and several conclusions rest on a single study. These findings are hypothesis-generating rather than establishing sex as a confirmed driver of habenula dysfunction. Estrous cycle stage, baseline circuit-level sexual dimorphism, and sociocultural confounds are identified as testable moderators for future research.

title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
authors: Miao D, Hou Z, Ge Y, Qi H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome. METHODS: We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. RESULTS: Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. Discriminative performance varied across derivation and validation cohorts, with suboptimal external-validation results. All models had a high risk of bias per PROBAST (low concerns regarding applicability); therefore, their findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Quantitative risk assessment of Salmonella exposure along the chicken production-to-consumption chain in China combined with meta-analysis.
authors: Xu C, Bian Z, Kan Z, Ding L, Wang B, Chen X, Kang X, Jiao X
abstract: Salmonella transmission along the broiler production chain represents a significant route for foodborne illness in humans. China exhibits regional disparities in foodborne salmonellosis, yet the specific contribution of chicken consumption to human exposure across different Salmonella serotypes remains unclear. To bridge this gap, a farm-to-fork quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA) framework was developed. The meta-analysis of currently available data showed that the representative estimate of Salmonella prevalence on Chinese broiler farms was 7.17% (95% CI: 4.74-10.70%). Incorporating the Beta-Poisson dose-response relationship, the model yielded a baseline relative risk estimate of 2.99 × 106 (95% CI: 1.27 × 106-5.79 × 106) chicken-attributable salmonellosis cases per year in China. Sensitivity analysis identified chilling, scalding, and Salmonella load on cutting knives as critical control points. In the ranking based on farm-level prevalence, Salmonella Enteritidis had the highest relative risk estimate. In the ranking based on the proportion of resistant strains, ampicillin had the highest relative risk estimate, corresponding to an estimated 2.39 × 106 annual cases. However, this estimate was based on a limited number of studies and should be interpreted with caution. Scenario analyses showed that replacing sodium hypochlorite with peracetic acid during chilling reduced the risk of illness by 24.09%. Increasing the separation rate of raw and cooked utensils to 75% during household handling reduced the estimated annual number of cases by approximately 51%.

title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
authors: Ng WL, Xu Y, Liu F, Bartolo P
abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice.
authors: Nobile B, Courtet P
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Molecular arrangements of Thionine within the DNA scaffolds enable machine learning-assisted colorimetric LAMP detection.
authors: Sharma AS, Yuk AY, Lee H, Lee NY
abstract: In the present work, we describe the distinctive molecular arrangement behavior of the phenothiazine dye - thionine (Th) - in the presence of LAMP amplicons and demonstrate its potential use as a visual indicator for LAMP-based detection. To better understand the mechanism responsible for DNA-templated stacking of Th molecules, detailed photophysical investigations were carried out in the presence of DNA and poly(acrylic acid) (PAA). Molecular docking analysis using AutoDock suggested that the planar phenothiazine aromatic core of Th is positioned along the groove region with the -NH2 groups oriented toward the outer region of the groove, remaining partially exposed to the solvent. Taking advantage of this interaction behavior, Th was further utilized to develop a colorimetric assay for nucleic acid amplification using LAMP. The dye exhibited a distinct color transition from violet to blue in the presence of LAMP amplicons generated by targeting the pneumolysin (ply) gene of Streptococcus pneumoniae. This visual change was accompanied by a bathochromic shift in the absorption spectrum, indicating DNA-induced molecular arrangements of Th molecules. The developed Th-based LAMP assay showed a limit of detection of 0.1 pg/μL. In addition, a machine learning-assisted image analysis approach was explored to quantitatively evaluate the colorimetric responses under standardized imaging conditions.

title: DCDA-Net: A depthwise convolution dilated attention network with temporal weighted loss for seizure prediction.
authors: Dong X, Li H, Chen Q, Chen X, Lu W, He L, Tin C, Zhou W
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: The sudden and unforeseeable nature of seizures poses serious threats to patients' safety and quality of daily life, making the development of highly accurate and reliable seizure prediction methods of significant clinical importance. To this end, this study proposed a seizure prediction model by integrating depthwise convolution and a novel dilated attention mechanism, named DCDA-Net. Depthwise convolution was first employed to extract features from each EEG channel independently, preserving spatial channel information for subsequent seizure evolution analysis. Innovatively combining dilated convolution with self-attention mechanisms, a dilated attention module was devised to efficiently capture long-range temporal dependencies. Furthermore, a temporal weighted loss function was introduced to significantly enhance the model's ability to discriminate critical preictal temporal features. Validation results on the CHB-MIT and SH-SDU clinical databases demonstrated that the model achieved a segment-based accuracy of 97.56% and an event-based sensitivity of 97.69% with a false prediction rate of 0.0232/hour on the CHB-MIT database, while attaining a segment-based accuracy of 96.93% and an event-based sensitivity of 96.05% on the SH-SDU database. Additionally, channel importance analysis confirmed significant spatial consistency with the actual epileptogenic zones. This study offered an efficient solution for patient-specific seizure prediction, with substantial potential for further clinical assessment.

title: PEGylated fucoxanthin liposomes remodel G0/G1 cell cycle homeostasis and suppress gallbladder cancer progression via modulation of NR2F1-mediated signaling networks.
authors: Cao JF, Hang K, Zhang X, Xia Q, Xia Z, Liao D, Rong C, Li K
abstract: PURPOSE: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is a highly aggressive and refractory biliary malignancy with disordered proliferative homeostasis, rapid malignant progression and scarce effective clinical therapies. Marine fucoxanthin possesses prominent anti-tumor activity, whereas its poor water solubility and low bioavailability limit application, and its core biomolecular mechanism against GBC remains poorly clarified. This study aimed to construct PEGylated fucoxanthin liposomes and elucidate their anti-tumor mechanism targeting biomolecular dynamics and core regulatory targets in GBC. METHODS: The anti-proliferative, anti-migratory, pro-apoptotic and cell cycle-regulatory effects of fucoxanthin-liposomes were verified using 2D monolayer and physiologically biomimetic 3D GBC spheroid models. Integrative transcriptomic analysis, multi-algorithm machine learning screening, RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence validation were performed to screen core functional targets. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were further conducted to confirm the stable binding characteristics between fucoxanthin and the target protein. RESULTS: Fucoxanthin-liposomes exerted significant dose-dependent inhibitory effects on GBC proliferation and migration, induced mitochondrial structural damage, extensive cell apoptosis, and robust G0/G1 cell cycle arrest. Multi-omics combined with machine learning identified NR2F1 as the pivotal target, whose expression was markedly upregulated after fucoxanthin-liposomes treatment. Fucoxanthin could stably bind NR2F1 through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions with excellent thermodynamic stability. CONCLUSION: PEGylated fucoxanthin liposomes restored G0/G1 quiescence-dominated cellular homeostasis and reversed pathological proliferative imbalance in GBC via transcriptional activation of NR2F1. Upregulated NR2F1 remodeled tumor proliferative homeostasis by hierarchically modulating PI3K/AKT/mTOR and JAK2/STAT3 signaling networks, and ultimately restrained GBC clonal proliferation and invasive progression.

title: A tunable brain-targeted PEGylated ginsenoside Rg1 derivative disrupts the ROS-mediated inflammasome-pyroptosis cascade to ameliorate Alzheimer's cognitive deficits.
authors: Zhu X, Liang H, Fan L, Bo J, Diao F, Qian Y, Zhang G, Li W
abstract: The pathogenic cascade of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and pyroptosis serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although ginsenoside Rg1 exhibits pleiotropic neuroprotective activities, its poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability severely hinders its clinical translation. To overcome this limitation, a brain-targeted delivery system was constructed using a covalent conjugation strategy, linking purified Rg1 with rhodamine B-modified polyethylene glycol (PEG) of varying chain lengths (Rg1s-PEG). After screening, the derivative Rg1s-PEG-600 was identified as achieving an optimal balance between hydrophilic stealth properties and steric hindrance, demonstrating enhanced brain accumulation and favorable biosafety profiles. In both in vitro and in vivo models of lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation, Rg1s-PEG-600 attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, inhibited canonical neuronal pyroptosis mediated by the NLRP1/3 inflammasomes, and significantly ameliorated behavioral deficits and synaptic loss. Furthermore, in chronic 5xFAD transgenic mice, systemic administration of Rg1s-PEG-600 for 12 weeks markedly reversed spatial memory decline, anxiety-like behavior, and synaptic protein depletion. Mechanistic studies further revealed that this targeted nanotherapeutic not only suppressed the ROS-NLRP1 signaling axis and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis in the AD brain but also comprehensively inhibited amyloidogenesis and Tau hyperphosphorylation. This work provides a promising, multitarget nanotherapeutic strategy to overcome BBB limitations and disrupt the complex pathological networks underlying neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Maternal piromelatine treatment is associated with attenuated behavioral alterations and sex-specific changes in hippocampal pCREB/BDNF signaling in adult offspring following prenatal constant-light exposure.
authors: Stoyanova T, Ivanova P, Tchekalarova J
abstract: Maternal exposure to constant light during pregnancy (CLE) is associated with disrupted circadian organization and persistent behavioral alterations in adult offspring. This study examined behavioural performance and 24-hour locomotor activity patterns, as well as hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels, in adult male and female offspring following prenatal CLE and maternal treatment with piromelatine (pir), which acts as an agonist at melatonin MT1/MT2 and serotonin 5-HT1A/5-HT1D receptors. Pregnant Wistar rats under light-dark regime received vehicle (veh), whereas dams exposed to CLE received vehicle (LL-veh), pir (10 mg/kg), or melatonin. Compared to the LL-veh groups, offspring from pir-treated dams exhibited reduced anxiety- and depression-like responses and improved working memory in both sexes. Individual-subject cosinor analysis revealed heterogeneous 24-hour locomotor rhythmicity within and between groups. No significant treatment-group effect was detected for MESOR or amplitude, and the descriptive acrophase patterns did not provide evidence of treatment-induced restoration or normalization of circadian organization. Maternal pir treatment was associated with higher hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels in male, but not female offspring relative to the LL-veh group. While the behavioral and molecular differences occurred concurrently in males, these findings do not prove that pCREB/BDNF signaling mediated the behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, the study cannot distinguish the direct developmental effects of maternal pir exposure from those mediated through maternal or offspring circadian rhythm. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as long-term behavioral and sex-specific molecular differences associated with maternal pir treatment rather than as evidence of circadian-independent antidepressant, anxiolytic, cognitive-enhancing, or BDNF-enhancing actions.

title: Functional remodeling of the maternal brain: Linking brain c-Fos dynamics to behavioral changes in pregnancy: An exploratory study.
authors: Yang L, Shang Y, Liu X, Wang J, Zhang H, Yang L
abstract: As an exploratory study with a limited sample size, this work systematically examined pregnancy-induced changes in neural activity by analyzing c-Fos expression across the whole brain of pregnant mice. The results showed that 36 brain regions-including the cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, and hypothalamus-exhibited dynamic changes in c-Fos expression throughout pregnancy. Behavioral tests revealed that pregnant mice displayed increased anxiety-like behavior in the elevated plus maze. Group-level descriptive correlation analysis indicated nominal directional trends between regional c-Fos expression and anxiety-related behavior, but no associations remained statistically significant after multiple testing correction. Furthermore, comparison with human prenatal brain imaging data suggested that adaptive changes in the hippocampus and hypothalamus are conserved across species. These preliminary findings provide initial insights into understanding brain adaptation during pregnancy, and require validation in larger cohort studies.

title: Screening a thermotolerant Komagataella phaffii strain with methanol cross-tolerance and the associated physiological and transcriptional responses.
authors: Li C, Jiang T, Bo Y, Lu Z, Zhou Y, Zhang G
abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a prominent methylotrophic yeast widely used in industrial biotechnology for heterologous protein production, chemical synthesis, and C1 feedstock utilization. However, its industrial application is limited by thermal stress and methanol toxicity, while the relationship between heat adaptation and methanol tolerance remains poorly understood. Here, we obtained a thermotolerant mutant ATH through ARTP mutagenesis followed by adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under heat stress (37 °C). ATH tolerated heat and methanol robustly under individual stress conditions, achieving 3-fold and 8-fold higher cell densities than GS115 at 37 °C or in 5% (v/v) methanol, respectively, yet failed under the combined stress of 37 °C and 5% methanol. Using three proteins (GFP, OPH, and ChiA) as reporters, we found that ATH showed higher heterologous expression than GS115 at 33 °C. Physiologically, ATH displayed enhanced cell wall/membrane integrity, reduced ROS accumulation and lower lipid peroxidation (>30% reduction in MDA), and accelerated formaldehyde clearance. Transcriptomics identified 561 shared differentially expressed genes, with coordinated upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSP70/40/90 families; Hsp104 and Hsp70-SSA2), antioxidant enzymes (catalase, peroxiredoxin), and cell wall/membrane remodeling genes, alongside downregulation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. Whole-genome resequencing further distinguished ATH from GS115 by only 19 variants (9 SNPs and 10 InDels), highlighting a compact genetic basis for the evolved phenotype. This work provides a K. phaffii chassis with improved individual heat and methanol tolerance and elucidates the physiological, transcriptional, and genomic mechanism underlying heat-methanol cross-adaptation.

title: Liquid contactable colorimetric sensor array for bacteria discrimination.
authors: Kim YM, Lee MG, Kim SH, Shin DI, Lee JH, Kim J, Lim SH, Yi GR
abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of bacterial metabolites in liquid culture is critical for early diagnosis of sepsis, yet conventional dye-based colorimetric sensor arrays (CSAs) are hindered by dye leaching and poor interfacial interactions in aqueous environments. Here, we introduce a polydimethylsiloxane-based CSA (PDMS-CSA) platform that overcomes these limitations by leveraging the intrinsic hydrophobicity of PDMS to stably immobilize water-soluble indicator dyes within the polymer matrix. This design ensures direct, unimpeded contact between analytes and sensors, enhancing both sensitivity and reproducibility. The PDMS matrix further contributes by preventing dye leaching while facilitating mass transport of bacterial metabolites such as ammonia (500 μM), hydrogen sulfide (50 μM), and carbon dioxide (1.7 mM) to the immobilized indicators, thereby enabling rapid and robust colorimetric responses. Using this platform, we achieved reliable differentiation between cocci and bacilli within 3 h, demonstrating a capability for rapid, clinically relevant bacterial identification. By combining operational simplicity with high analytical performance in complex liquid media, PDMS-CSAs represent a transformative approach for point-of-care sepsis diagnostics. Beyond sepsis, this strategy offers a versatile framework for the development of next-generation, non-invasive microbial sensor operating platforms with broad translational potential in clinical and environmental monitoring.

title: Behavioural avoidance to imagined conditioned stimuli in differential fear conditioning.
authors: Mitra S, Lyons AL, Hajiloo M, Greening SG
abstract: The underlying mechanisms of how a fear is born in our imagination is presently unclear. The current study used differential fear conditioning to assess how a fear is created in one's mind and how behavioural avoidance interacts with imagined fear. This study contained an Acquisition, Behavioural Avoidance, and Transfer phase. During the Acquisition phase, participants combined instructions such that whether they heard "imagine yellow" (colour instruction) or "imagine horizontal" (orientation instruction) they were to imagine yellow horizontal lines (CS+) and likewise for the "imagine blue" and "imagine vertical" instructions (CS-). Unbeknownst to participants, they only received the mild shock (US) to the orientation instructions. This manipulation allowed for a disambiguation of descriptive and depictive elements of how imagination interacts with fear. Next, participants completed the Behavioural Avoidance phase, whereby participants had the option to avoid the US after hearing the trial's instructions. Finally, in the Transfer phase, participants were visually shown the CS+ and CS- to determine how their fear transferred from imagery to perception. Self-report, skin conductance response (SCR), and behavioural avoidance attempts were used as dependent measures. Results from each phase and dependent measure suggested that fear was driven by the orientation instructions. Furthermore, fear was shown to transfer from imagery to the corresponding visual stimuli. In this way, these results suggest that both depictive and descriptive elements are involved in the creation of fears in our imagination.

title: Preliminary experience with controlled hypothermic storage of donor heart in combined heart transplantation.
authors: Argaw ST, Lora Ronco L, Frering A, Kloeckner M, Coutance G, Coilly A, Vibert E, Snanoudj R
abstract: While studies have demonstrated improved clinical outcomes with the use of controlled hypothermic storage (CHS) devices in isolated heart transplantation, it has not been evaluated in combined heart transplantation. In this small retrospective study (n=17), we evaluate clinical outcomes after combined heart-liver and heart-kidney transplantation in recipients of donor hearts preserved with conventional ice cold storage (ICS, n=10) versus CHS (n=7). The study found severe early graft dysfunction (EGD) occurred more frequently in the ICS cohort when compared to the CHS cohort (70% vs 0%, respectively). In addition, the CHS cohort had shorter median intensive care unit length of stay (7 days compared to 15.5 days, respectively) as well as fewer post-transplant complications, including sepsis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS), pneumonia (40% in ICS and 14.3% in CHS), stroke (30% in ICS and 0% in CHS), and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis (60% in ICS and 28.6% in CHS). These preliminary findings suggest CHS may improve outcomes in combined heart transplantation.

title: Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) Mapping and Visualization of Pre-Implementation Determinants for Sepsis Care Transitions.
authors: You SB, Stawnychy MA, Song J, Hirschman KB, O'Connor M, Sang E, Oh S, Pitcher K
abstract: INTRODUCTION: High-quality care transitions are essential for sepsis survivors at risk of readmission and long-term complications. These complex innovations require coordination across organizations, individuals, and processes. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) offers a systematic approach to identifying multi-level implementation determinants, but translating them into actionable strategies remains challenging. This study examines the representation of implementation determinants across CFIR domains and visualizes their cross-domain interconnectedness. METHODS: CFIR-guided, semi-structured pre-implementation needs assessment interviews were conducted with stakeholders involved in sepsis care transitions across five hospital-home healthcare (HHC) dyads. Thirty-two themes identified through deductive-inductive coding were mapped to CFIR domains and constructs and visualized using node diagrams. RESULTS: Sixty-one interviews with 91 stakeholders identified 32 themes spanning all five CFIR domains, with most themes mapping to multiple domains. Access to Care theme mapped across all five domains, while External Policies and Incentives and Informal Caregiving themes were represented only once. Implementation Process domain was most represented and Innovation least represented. All constructs within the Implementation Process and Individual Characteristics domains were captured. Node diagrams illustrated the depth and interconnected influence of determinants in sepsis care transitions. CONCLUSIONS: Stakeholders identified complexity emerged across technical, structural, and policy domains as both an innovation feature and contextual determinants of sepsis care transitions. CFIR mapping and visualization provided a structured approach to characterizing pre-implementation complexity in sepsis care transitions. Examining determinant representation and cross-domain interconnectedness may help identify cross-cutting, potentially high-leverage implementation needs and inform strategy selection and tailoring for complex hospital-to-home interventions.

Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging.
authors: Wu JW, Wang YK, Mukundan A, Karmakar R, Nhu NNQ, Nagisetti Y, Liao WC, Han ML
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) detection is crucial for improving survival. While narrow-band imaging (NBI) improves mucosal visualization, limitations remain. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE), an algorithmic NBI-like technology reconstructed from white light imaging (WLI). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, image-based exploratory feasibility study to descriptively evaluate the diagnostic performance of WLI, NBI, and SAVE. A dataset of 1350 still endoscopic images (450 each for WLI, NBI, and SAVE) across normal mucosa, dysplasia, and ESCC stages from 158 patients was blindly reviewed by three endoscopists with different experience levels (3, 5, and 15 years). Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and reading time. RESULTS: For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. Mean per-image reading times were similar across WLI, NBI, and SAVE. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study, SAVE showed diagnostic potential for ESCC, with observed diagnostic performance metrics numerically similar to those of WLI and NBI in this exploratory dataset, but lacked sensitivity for dysplasia. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further prospective, multicenter validation to refine the algorithm for early cancer detection.

title: Age-structured two-sex HPV transmission dynamics with a carrier state and reactivation.
authors: Shao S, Guo T, Gao S
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) remains one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide, and its persistence and possible reactivation complicate efforts to understand and control transmission. In particular, the presence of a carrier stage and variation in reactivation across age and sex may play important roles in maintaining HPV prevalence. In this paper, we develop a two-sex Susceptible-Infectious-Carrying-Recovered (SICR) model with n discrete age groups to investigate how age-specific and sex-specific reactivation rates affect HPV transmission dynamics and how control measures can be designed accordingly. We derive the basic reproduction number  R 0   and show that it provides a threshold criterion for disease elimination. The existence and stability of both the disease-free equilibrium and the endemic equilibrium are established rigorously. Using epidemiological data from Hangzhou in 2011, we estimate  R 0   to be 2.177. Analytical and numerical results show that viral reactivation plays an important role in sustaining HPV endemicity and highlight the need for age-specific and sex-specific public health strategies. We also find that an excessively low viral reactivation rate is not always beneficial for controlling HPV prevalence. In particular, regulating reactivation alone is insufficient to control HPV transmission effectively, and our results suggest that combined interventions targeting both transmission and reactivation are more effective.

title: Seasonal dynamic model for projecting tuberculosis epidemiological trends in Kyrgyzstan.
authors: Altynai B, Lou P, Gulmira K, Shauer D, Xu J, Wang K
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health burden in Kyrgyzstan; however, the seasonal transmission dynamics of TB in the country have not been quantitatively characterized. This study aimed to develop a seasonal dynamic model to simulate TB transmission, estimate the basic reproduction number R 0, assess transmission intensity, and inform evidence-based prevention and control strategies. Using monthly reported new TB cases from the national TB surveillance and registration system in Kyrgyzstan from 2022 to 2025, we constructed a seasonal SEIR model incorporating periodic transmission and reactivation rates. Model parameters were estimated using a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. R 0 was calculated using two methods: the periodic time-varying method and the annual average transmission rate method. Local sensitivity analysis was performed to evaluate the impact of the baseline transmission parameter a s and the baseline reactivation parameter a e on TB transmission dynamics. The model adequately captured the seasonal fluctuations and overall downward trend in new TB cases, achieving a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 8.66% and a root mean square percentage error (RMSPE) of 9.95%. The estimated periodic R 0 was 0.8842 (95% credible interval [CrI]: 0.8811-0.8873), which remained below the threshold of unity. Assuming no change in current prevention and control measures, projections suggest a gradual decline in monthly new TB cases, with the annual number of new cases declining to approximately 2902 by 2126. These results indicate that TB transmission has not been fully interrupted and that elimination is unlikely to be achieved within the projection period. Sensitivity analysis revealed that both a s and a e substantially affected the number of new TB cases and R 0, and that modest changes in these parameters could drive R 0 above the threshold of unity. The seasonal SEIR model provided a good fit to the monthly number of new TB cases in Kyrgyzstan. Although the estimated R 0 is below the threshold of unity, indicating a declining epidemic trend, the rate of decline remains relatively slow, highlighting the need to sustain and strengthen prevention and control measures.

title: Environmental Impact of Conventional Versus Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Colorectal Lesions: A Procedure-Based Life Cycle Assessment With Pooled Effectiveness Estimates.
authors: Calabrese G, Moll F, Neves JAC, Bonacci L, Sinagra E, Castiglione F, Maida M, Albéniz-Arbizu E
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The environmental impact of endoscopic techniques remains poorly defined. We compared procedure-related environmental outcomes between conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and underwater EMR (U-EMR) for colorectal lesions. METHODS: In this prospective pilot procedure-based life cycle assessment of the resection phase, 10-25-mm colorectal lesions underwent EMR or U-EMR across three endoscopy units. Outcomes included global warming potential (GWP, kg CO2-equivalent/procedure), waste, life-cycle water consumption, fossil resource scarcity, and terrestrial acidification. Exploratory GWP per en bloc resection was estimated using pooled randomized-trial and pilot-cohort data. RESULTS: Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. En bloc resection was achieved in 56.5% of EMR and 69.2% of U-EMR, and R0 resection in 52.2% and 69.2%. Mean GWP was significantly lower with U-EMR than EMR (1.92 ± 0.54 vs. 2.42 ± 0.50 kg CO2-eq; p = 0.002), corresponding to a reduction of 0.50 kg CO2-eq per procedure and 50 kg CO2-eq per 100 procedures. U-EMR was associated with lower waste generation (324.0 ± 78.3 vs. 407.3 ± 72.0 g; p < 0.001), water consumption (0.56 ± 0.17 vs. 0.77 ± 0.20 m3; p < 0.001), fossil resource scarcity (0.33 ± 0.10 vs. 0.40 ± 0.09 kg oil-eq; p = 0.007), and terrestrial acidification (0.0052 ± 0.0018 vs. 0.0068 ± 0.0018 kg SO2-eq; p = 0.003). Findings were consistent across scenario and uncertainty analyses. In the meta-analysis-based model, GWP per en bloc resection was lower with U-EMR than EMR (2.59 vs. 3.51 kg CO2-eq), corresponding to a 26.3% relative reduction. CONCLUSIONS: U-EMR was associated with lower procedure-related environmental burden than conventional EMR, persisting after normalization for en bloc resection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: No. 165/26.

title: Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
authors: Kamada H, Kobayashi K, Yamana H, Fujita N, Namima D, Yamada M, Fujita S, Suto H
abstract: During peroral cholangioscopy-guided electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL), stone fragmentation obscures the visual field (the "snowstorm effect"), and visualization quality has been assessed only subjectively. This proof-of-concept study explored the feasibility of a deep-learning method for objectively quantifying visualization quality during EHL and, as an exploratory application, compared viscous gel immersion with saline irrigation. A ResNet-18 model was trained on expert-annotated frames (5-point scale) from three development cases. For independent validation, 120 frames from 12 previously unseen comparison cases were scored by two blinded endoscopists (inter-reader weighted κ = 0.98). The model showed only moderate agreement with their consensus (weighted κ = 0.60; accuracy 70.8%); because the validation sample was enriched for predicted-usable frames, metrics re-weighted to the natural frame distribution gave sensitivity 29.8% and specificity 93.5%, indicating systematic under-detection of usable views. Agreement did not differ systematically between gel and saline frames. The High-Quality View Rate (HQVR) was the proportion of EHL-phase frames scored Good/Excellent. In a patient-level comparison, median HQVR was 22.7% for gel versus 8.4% for saline (exact Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.15, not significant); in post hoc exploratory analyses, a threshold-independent mean predicted score differed (1.65 vs. 1.35, p = 0.005) and the longest continuous usable interval favored gel (median 24.4 vs. 5.2 s). Mild cholangitis occurred in 1/5 gel and 4/7 saline patients. Training such a model is feasible, but it is not yet a validated measurement tool, and the gel-versus-saline signal is hypothesis-generating only. Larger multi-case training and prospective validation are required. Trial Registration: N/A.

title: Echo-DM: Ultrasound marker removal via conditional latent diffusion and region-aware fusion.
authors: Wang Z, Huang T, Jiang W, Li M, Liu J, Chen J, Zou J, Luo Y
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Clinical ultrasound images often contain artificial markers, such as measurement calipers and text, to assist diagnostic interpretation and comparison. However, these markers can introduce shortcut bias in downstream automated analysis, encouraging deep learning models to rely on marker-related cues rather than clinically meaningful anatomy. Existing marker removal methods are either mask-dependent and vulnerable to error propagation, or mask-free deterministic restorers that may over-smooth ultrasound texture and perturb unaffected background regions. To address these challenges, we present Echo-DM, a framework for ultrasound marker removal via conditional latent diffusion and region-aware fusion. Echo-DM follows a generate-select-refine formulation: a DiT-based Conditional Latent Diffusion Network (CLDN) generates an intermediate restoration, and a Region-Aware Fusion (RAF) module internally predicts a soft map to selectively fuse the restoration with intact input content before residual refinement in image space under end-to-end mask-free inference. The image-space RAF is latent-module-agnostic and is shared by Echo-DM-V and Echo-DM-R, which use VAE-based and RAE-based latent modules, respectively. Extensive experiments on Echo-PAIR, a large-scale paired clinical ultrasound dataset, demonstrate superior marker removal and strong anatomical fidelity compared with representative two-stage baselines, while providing favorable quality-efficiency trade-offs across deployment settings. Code and models will be released at Echo-DM.
